newsitem.title: USA: White cops charged in death of black man are tried.
newsitem.headline: White cops charged in death of black man are tried.

text.p: Two white policemen charged in the death of a black motorist went on trial Tuesday before an all-white jury in a case that has raised racial tensions.

The trial of Brentwood Lt. Milton Mulholland, 57, and Baldwin Patrolman Michael Albert, 32, is expected to last about two weeks in common pleas court. They are charged with one count each of involuntary manslaughter in the suffocation death of Jonny Gammage, 31, who was a cousin and business partner of Pittsburgh Steelers defensive lineman Ray Seals.
The jury consists of nine women and three men. Jurors were picked in Chester County in eastern Pennsylvania because of extensive publicity about the case.
Brentwood and Baldwin are Pittsburgh suburbs. Gammage died last October on a roadside in another suburb, Overbrook, after he was pulled over by Mulholland.
The officers testified in a coroner's inquest that he was driving erratically and became violent when he got out of his car. They said they were forced to restrain him by holding him on the ground.
The cause of death was ruled as suffocation caused by compression to the chest.
A third officer who was at the scene and also charged in the incident, Brentwood Patrolman John Vojtas, 40, will be tried separately. A jury has not yet been selected.
